findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide how `tests/live_jira_dc/` tests are isolated from the *CI integration tier* (`pytest -m integration` in `_build-and-test.yml:447`): either add a skip-unless-docker-available guard in the fixture, use a sub-marker expression (e.g. `integration and not dc_harness`), or document that this is accepted and the CI step will skip gracefully — and update the `_build-and-test.yml` comment that says 'These need no live services.'
evidence: Plan states: 'Every test in the directory carries the existing `integration` marker — not a new custom marker — because `make test` runs `pytest -m "not integration and not external"` ... so the suite is excluded by construction with no Makefile change'
_build-and-test.yml:447 runs `pytest -m integration` as a named CI step: 'Run the integration tier (concurrency + reconciler; network-guarded)'
test_ci_workflow_parity.py:68 asserts `"integration tier": "pytest -m integration"` must appear in CI gates
The integration tier step's own comment says 'These need no live services (mocked acli / local git)' — an assumption J5's tests would violate
findings.finding: The plan treats `pytest -m "not integration and not external"` exclusion as full CI isolation, but `_build-and-test.yml:447` runs `pytest -m integration` as a separate CI step on every commit. Integration-marked tests in `tests/live_jira_dc/` will be collected and executed in that CI step, which requires a running Docker daemon, a live container, and egress to `maven.atlassian.com` — none of which are available on standard CI runners. The CI workflow is an unenumerated consumer whose behavior J5 changes.
findings.location: Scope section / Testing section / AC 'gating oracle' bullet; _build-and-test.yml:447
scenarios: Every PR and main-branch push runs _build-and-test.yml, which executes `pytest -m integration`. After J5 lands, that step will attempt to connect to a Jira container that doesn't exist on the CI runner, causing connection failures or skips that produce misleading green results.
The CI comment 'network-guarded' is misleading — the integration tier is not network-guarded at the conftest level; that guard covers only unit/ and scripts/.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a session-scoped fixture or a module-level skip guard in `tests/live_jira_dc/conftest.py` that checks whether the Jira container is reachable and calls `pytest.skip('jira-dc harness not running')` at collection time. This converts a hard failure into an explicit skip in the CI integration step, and documents the behavior. Alternatively, introduce a `dc_harness` sub-marker and filter it from the CI integration run with `pytest -m 'integration and not dc_harness'`, updating `_build-and-test.yml` and `test_ci_workflow_parity.py` accordingly.

findings.finding: The adapter code overwhelmingly uses `/rest/api/3/` endpoints (issue reads, transitions, label updates, search via `POST /rest/api/3/search/jql` with Cloud-only `nextPageToken` cursor pagination) that do not exist on Jira Server/DC 8.x, which exposes only `/rest/api/2/`. The plan states the harness 'proves REST v2 protocol semantics' and the teardown oracle polls `/rest/api/2/issue/{key}`, but the adapter code paths that would actually run against this harness (`acli_graph.py` search/JQL, `acli_rest.py` transitions/updates, `acli_cli_ops.py` issue reads) all target `/rest/api/3/` and would fail with 404 on the target instance. A future implementer runs the adapter's reconcile pass against the harness and hits 404 on the search endpoint, producing confusing failures that are attributed to the harness rather than the API version gap.

On GitHub Actions hosted runners, CircleCI, shared Jenkins agents, and similar environments, any process in the same job or a co-scheduled job can connect to loopback ports, and the well-known admin/admin credentials make this exploitable without any brute-force.

Mitigations: (a) run only on dedicated single-tenant runners, OR (b) have the fixture immediately change the admin password via the Jira REST API at startup and restore or destroy the instance at teardown.' findings.finding: The teardown oracle asserts each delete call's HTTP status is 2xx and then polls for 404, but the plan specifies no retry or escalation path when a delete returns a non-2xx status — leaving the error-handling contract for write operations incomplete.

findings.finding: J5 redefines the image acquisition mechanism in a way that directly contradicts the parent's explicit instruction. The parent (e369, Approach step 5) specifies `docker run -dit -p 2990:2990 pycontribs/jira-test-image:8.17.1` — a pull-and-run model — as the harness substrate. J5 explicitly states this formulation is 'false' and instead delivers a build-from-vendored-Dockerfile mechanism using the addono base image. Even though J5's factual correction is sound, under G7 the parent wins on any conflict; a leaf may not silently redefine a parent deliverable. The parent's plan must be updated first to replace the `docker run pycontribs/jira-test-image:8.17.1` instruction with the verified build-from-Dockerfile approach, staling the parent's plan-review attestation and requiring re-review, before J5 can be treated as a pure subset.

findings.finding: The Approach section describes mounting a persistent Maven cache volume as a design requirement ('the fixture SHOULD mount a persistent Maven cache (~/.m2) as a volume, or every fresh container re-downloads ~900 artifacts'), but neither the Scope section nor any AC line covers this deliverable. The SHOULD makes it advisory, yet the Approach frames it as the remedy for a concrete operational problem (~900 artifacts re-downloaded on every fresh container). Without an AC or Scope entry, an implementer can omit it without failing any criterion, producing a harness that is technically compliant but painfully slow in practice.
findings.location: Approach section ('The fixture SHOULD mount a persistent Maven cache') vs Scope section (compose file bullet, no volume mentioned) and AC section (no criterion for Maven cache volume)
scenarios: Implementer skips the volume mount because no AC requires it; CI runs re-download 900 artifacts on every execution, making the harness too slow to be useful on cold runners
